entries.title: Job 27:1
segments: Parable; a representation from which moral instruction may be drawn.

entries.title: Job 27:2
segments: Taken away my judgment; refused to justify him, or appear to do so, by removing his calamities.

entries.title: Job 27:4
segments: Not speak wickedness; by condemning himself as a hypocrite, or approving the doctrine of his friends.

entries.title: Job 27:5
segments: Will not remove mine integrity; the same as, I will hold fast my righteousness,

.  Job means that, as he is conscious of having led an upright life, and of being still determined to do so, he will never acknowledge the justice of the accusations which his friends bring against him. 
 
Conscious integrity will give confidence in God, and support the soul under the sorest trials; but the want of it will deprive one of rest and peace.

entries.title: Job 27:7
segments: As the wicked--as the unrighteous; Job by no means approved of the wicked; though he contended, in opposition to his friends, that they were sometimes prosperous in this world.

entries.title: Job 27:8
segments: Though he hath gained; the reputation of being pious, or ever so much worldly good.  But some render, "when he shall be cut off," which agrees with the following clause, "when God taketh away his soul."

entries.title: Job 27:10
segments: Delight in the Almighty will be manifested by habitual communion with him; while neglect of communion with God, is evidence of want of love to him and to his ways.

entries.title: Job 27:11
segments:
I will teach you; teach you the true doctrine concerning the wicked. 
 
  By the hand of God; or, concerning the hand of God.

entries.title: Job 27:12
segments: Seen it; seen illustrations of the truth in the facts of divine Providence.

entries.title: Job 27:13
segments: This is the portion of a wicked man; at first sight, the description of Job,

, seems to agree altogether with that of the three friends.  Hence many interpreters have understood it as spoken in their name, thus: "Why then are ye thus altogether vain, [saying,] 'This is the portion of a wicked man,'" etc.  But Job undertakes,

, to teach his friends concerning God's providence, and these verses appear to contain his doctrine.  It differs from that of his friends in this important respect, that according to them, calamity always speedily overtakes the wicked, and is sent only as a punishment for wickedness; while Job's position is, that good and bad men are both alike subject to calamities; and yet the final end of the ungodly must be destruction, while the good man, after he is tried, shall come forth as gold,

.  If at times he speaks as if he were sinking down under his sorrows, without the hope of ever again seeing good, we must remember that this is the language of impatience and unbelief, to which all believers are liable in the hour of severe trial.

entries.title: Job 27:19
segments:
Shall lie down; in death. 
 
  Be gathered; by an honorable funeral.  It is of a man who has gained his riches by wickedness that he speaks. 
 
  Openeth his eyes, and he is not; perishes in the twinkling of an eye.  This seems to be a proverbial expression.

entries.title: Job 27:22
segments: God shall cast upon him, and not spare; visit him with calamities. this is often the case in this world, and always in the world to come.
